terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Stylized camera estimate for the closed three-quarter concept. Use a separate orthographic-like overhead review for the open spread; compare by silhouette and feature placement rather than claiming metric camera recovery.

objectClass.notes: The closed concept is authoritative for outer silhouette, cloth, brass plate, page block, and fore-edge ribbon. The open journal concept is authoritative for the two page stacks, gutter, page crown, rules, paper fiber, open cover lip, and ribbon through the gutter. The hidden rear cover is a consistency inference: match the front cover's cloth wrap, thickness, corner radius, and edge construction, but omit the front nameplate and rivets.

reasoning: The closed object reads as a compact rounded volume, but opening it reveals two independent cover/page sides, a center hinge, and a continuous bookmark path.
Identity depends on repeated page-edge strata, faint ruled lines, two brass fasteners, and multi-band cloth/paper/ribbon relief rather than on a few primitive solids.
The front cover must rotate around the existing spine-side hinge while the root and interaction coordinates remain stable, so pivot placement is a fidelity and runtime requirement.
The rear exterior is not directly shown; symmetry and matching bookbinding construction are sufficient only for a stylized consistency inference, not an observed claim.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Closed and open states must share one stable hierarchy with named cover/page pivots, separate left/right page stacks, repeated page and rule systems, and independent cloth, paper, brass, and ribbon responses.

detailInventory.note: All detail claims come from the authoritative closed/open concepts. The neutral board only groups those crops. Hidden rear-cover treatment is explicitly marked as a consistency inference.

details.description: Front cover has broad plan-view corner arcs and a softly rolled cloth-wrapped edge; the radius must be authored in the cover plane rather than clamped by its thin thickness.
details.scale: meso; corner radius about 5 percent of cover width with a 3-4 segment edge roll
details.affects: front-cover silhouette and grazing rim highlight

details.description: Dense directional cloth ribs cross the moss-green cover and break highlights into fine parallel strands.
details.scale: micro; approximately 35-55 visible ribs per cover width at close review distance
details.affects: cloth normal, roughness, and anisotropic highlight breakup

details.description: A slightly compressed darker cloth line follows the wrapped cover perimeter inside the rolled edge.
details.scale: micro-to-meso; recessed line about 0.8 percent of cover width
details.affects: cover construction read and edge ambient occlusion

details.description: Two shallow vertical shoulder channels and a rounded convex spine separate the binding from the front cover plane.
details.scale: meso; two narrow grooves flanking a spine about 5 percent of closed-book width
details.affects: spine silhouette, hinge readability, and cavity shadow

details.description: The blank brass plate is a thin rounded rectangle with a real chamfer that produces a bright warm rim.
details.scale: meso; plate about 30 percent of cover width and 9 percent of cover height
details.affects: nameplate silhouette and metallic edge highlight

details.description: Two raised domed brass rivets sit symmetrically near the plate ends with visible contact shadows.
details.scale: micro; two hemispherical heads, each about 8 percent of plate length
details.affects: nameplate identity, repetition, and specular hotspots

details.description: The plate face carries mottled aged-brass color and roughness variation without green oxidation blooms.
details.scale: micro; low-amplitude irregular patches across the plate face
details.affects: brass albedo and roughness locality

details.description: The plate chamfer and rivet crowns are slightly more polished than the broad face and catch compact highlights.
details.scale: micro; low-roughness mask restricted to chamfer crests and rivet crowns
details.affects: brass roughness and clearcoat-like edge response

details.description: The closed ivory page block has a softly bowed fore-edge and rounded corners recessed inside the cover overhang.
details.scale: macro-to-meso; page block inset about 3-5 percent from the cover perimeter
details.affects: closed silhouette and cover/page negative space

details.description: Many slightly irregular horizontal ivory/tan strata remain legible across the closed fore-edge and open page fans.
details.scale: micro repeated system; 12-18 visible grouped layers rather than one flat slab
details.affects: page-edge relief, ambient occlusion, and layered book identity

details.description: Ivory page faces show fine non-directional paper fibers and gentle tonal mottling under close review.
details.scale: micro; high-frequency low-amplitude normal with independent roughness noise
details.affects: paper highlight breakup and tactile matte response

details.description: Exposed page edges are slightly warmer and darker than the clean open page faces, especially inside the fan and near corners.
details.scale: meso local mask on edge-facing geometry only
details.affects: paper albedo, AO, and layered depth separation

details.description: The left page stack fans upward from the outer edge and curves downward into the center gutter, with staggered visible leaves.
details.scale: meso repeated stack; 7-10 grouped leaf edges with nonuniform offsets
details.affects: open left silhouette, stack volume, and gutter depth

details.description: The right page stack mirrors the binding logic but retains small independent leaf offsets rather than perfect geometric symmetry.
details.scale: meso repeated stack; 7-10 grouped leaf edges with deterministic offset variation
details.affects: open right silhouette, stack volume, and gutter depth

details.description: Both top pages have a broad shallow crown: elevated near the binding and gently settling toward the outer cover edges.
details.scale: macro-to-meso spline bend; peak rise about 2-3 percent of page width
details.affects: top-page normals, silhouette under grazing light, and open-book volume

details.description: A narrow shadowed V-shaped gutter separates the left and right top pages and remains visible alongside the ribbon.
details.scale: meso; recessed valley about 1.5 percent of full spread width
details.affects: open-state negative space, page attachment, and AO

details.description: Thin warm-gray horizontal ruled lines cross both page faces at restrained contrast and do not emboss the paper.
details.scale: micro repeated decal lines; six to eight visible lines per page at review framing
details.affects: page-face albedo only, retaining paper normal continuity

details.description: The burgundy ribbon carries narrow longitudinal woven ribs and a fibrous matte highlight.
details.scale: micro; 8-12 visible longitudinal ribs across the ribbon width in close-up
details.affects: ribbon normal, roughness, and directional highlight

details.description: The free ribbon tail ends in a centered V notch with two clean diagonal tips.
details.scale: meso silhouette cut; notch depth about 35 percent of ribbon width
details.affects: bookmark terminal silhouette

details.description: One continuous ribbon is anchored at the spine head, lies down the open center gutter, and exits the closed fore edge without intersecting the page block.
details.scale: macro state path; controlled curve with closed and open state poses
details.affects: state continuity, attachment, and recognizable burgundy accent

details.description: The moss cloth cover remains visible as a narrow rounded border around the open page spread, including a padded dip beneath the gutter.
details.scale: meso; 3-5 percent border around page perimeter
details.affects: open silhouette and cloth-paper separation

definitionOfDone: Closed state matches the compact rounded moss-cloth silhouette, recessed ivory page block, convex spine, blank aged-brass plate with two domed rivets, and burgundy V-notched tail.

Open state approaches 180 degrees around a stable spine-side cover pivot and presents separate left/right page stacks, a readable V-shaped gutter, broad page crowns, layered outer edges, and a narrow cloth cover lip.
One ribbon path remains attached at the spine and transitions coherently between closed fore-edge and open gutter poses without page intersection or teleporting endpoints.
Cloth, paper, brass, and ribbon use independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO evidence; woven/fibrous/metallic responses remain readable under neutral and grazing light.
Overall AI-vision fidelity is at least 0.85 and every critical semantic feature scores at least 0.82 from a matched reference/render comparison.

featureGroups.name: Blank aged-brass nameplate and rivets

featureGroups.name: Cloth, paper, brass, and ribbon PBR separation
qualityCriteria: Moss cloth has directional weave normal/roughness, compressed edge variation, and no glossy plastic response.

failureModes: one albedo map is reused for unrelated PBR channels
materials are distinguished only by flat color

antiShallowSpecRules: Do not implement a cover or page with RoundedBoxGeometry when its radius is clamped by the thin axis; use plan-view shape extrusion or deformed indexed geometry.
Do not collapse the left and right page stacks, top pages, gutter, covers, spine, plate, rivets, or ribbon into one inert mesh.
Do not infer a decorated back cover: hidden rear geometry must be labeled consistency inference and must omit unobserved plate, logo, text, straps, or hardware.
Do not accept a page block represented by one smooth slab; grouped leaf layers and edge offsets must remain visible in closed and open review views.
Do not accept a flat open spread; both top pages require spline crown geometry and a recessed center gutter.
Do not accept a ribbon without a spine socket, state control points, page clearance, and V-notched end geometry.
Do not pass material look-dev when cloth, paper, brass, or ribbon aliases albedo into roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass any visual stage below 0.85 overall or below 0.82 for any critical semantic feature.

mustMatch: closed rounded clothbound silhouette, convex spine, cover overhang, and recessed ivory page block
open left/right page stacks, curved top pages, narrow gutter, and visible cloth lip
stable root plus front-cover hinge at [-1.5, 0.3, 0] opening to 0.97 pi around local Z
blank chamfered brass plate with exactly two domed rivets
continuous burgundy ribbon from spine socket through open gutter to closed V-notched fore-edge tail
independent cloth, paper, brass, and ribbon albedo/roughness/height-normal/AO response
niceToHave: tiny low-contrast page-face stamp from the open concept
subtle deterministic variation between individual page leaf offsets

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a matched authoritative reference, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score >= 0.85, all critical features >= 0.82, layer scores, and mismatch critique before choosing continue.

screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Keep the factory root at local [0, 0, 0]; the application owns world placement [-0.65, 0.34, 0.25].
Keep front-cover-pivot at local [-1.5, 0.3, 0] with closed rotation 0 and open rotation 0.97 pi about local Z.
Parent the front cloth shell, its inner page stack, brass plate, and rivets beneath front-cover-pivot so they preserve relative attachment during opening.
Expose named closed/open state transforms for page stacks and ribbon control points; do not rebuild or replace the root during phase changes.
Use simplified compound box colliders for interaction and preserve the existing invisible app hit area independently of visual geometry.

assumptions: Consistency inference: the hidden rear exterior repeats the observed moss cloth, thickness, corner radius, wrap seam, and edge compression of the front cover but has no nameplate, rivets, text, logo, strap, or other unobserved decoration.
